bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar's Makhana Reaches Greece as APEDA Facilitates 1 MT Export from Purnea
bihar_raw_news.content: Top Stories of the Day Share DD India October 2, 2026 4:43 PM IST Bihar’s Makhana Reaches Greece as APEDA Facilitates 1 MT Export from Purnea Author: DD India The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority, APEDA, has facilitated the export of one metric tonne of popped or Phool Makhana from Purnea in Bihar to Greece. The consignment was flagged off from Purnea, marking another step towards expanding international market access for Bihar’s traditional Makhana and creating opportunities for better returns for farmers through export-oriented value chains. The consignment, sourced by Indo Global Export, Belouri, Purnea, is being exported to Greece through S. S Foods Exports Pvt. Ltd., New Delhi. The shipment will be transported from Mundra Port in India to Piraeus Port in Greece. According to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the export has resulted in higher price realisation compared with the prevailing domestic market selling price. This highlights the potential of international markets to create additional value for Makhana producers. The export-led market access is also expected to strengthen linkages between producers and international buyers and create opportunities for improved returns to farmers. India is the world’s leading producer of Makhana, with Bihar accounting for around 80 to 85 per cent of the country’s production. Makhana cultivation in the state covers more than 35,000 hectares across 10 districts. The sector is supported by technical interventions from Bihar Agricultural University, Sabour, and the ICAR-National Research Centre for Makhana, Darbhanga. The flag-off programme was chaired by Bihar Agriculture Minister Vijay Kumar Sinha. APEDA Chairman Abhishek Dev, Director of Horticulture in the Bihar Agriculture Department Abhishek Kumar, senior government officials and other stakeholders associated with the Makhana export value chain were also present. Addressing the gathering, Vijay Kumar Sinha said the export marked an important milestone for Bihar’s Makhana sector as the product continued to gain access to international markets. He said, “The export marks an important milestone for Bihar’s Makhana sector as the product continues to reach international markets.” Sinha said India exported more than 7,000 metric tonnes of Makhana and value-added Makhana products, valued at around USD 22 million, during 2025-26, across more than 20 international destinations. He also said the Government of Bihar was working towards an Agri Export Policy aimed at supporting farmers and improving their incomes through export promotion. The Minister highlighted the development of packhouses to support the Makhana export value chain and commended APEDA for its efforts to expand Makhana exports and improve farmer realisation. The export from Purnea to Greece is part of efforts to connect Bihar’s Makhana producers and exporters with international markets. Makhana, which has a strong traditional and cultural association with Bihar, has emerged as an important product in India’s agricultural export basket. APEDA has been facilitating market linkages and supporting exporters in taking Indian Makhana to international markets. Exports of Makhana are also expanding into European markets, providing opportunities for Indian producers to diversify beyond traditional destinations.

bihar_raw_news.title: Nitin Gadkari's ethanol challenge: 'Show me one damaged vehicle'; minister hits back at ...
bihar_raw_news.content: ET Online Nitin Gadkari on ethanol blending Union minister Nitin Gadkari has pushed back against concerns that ethanol-blended petrol can damage vehicles, challenging critics to produce evidence of vehicles being affected by the fuel. Speaking at the inaugural session of the Bihar Investor Summit 2026, Gadkari defended the Centre's ethanol-blending programme and said the policy was aimed not only at reducing dependence on conventional fuels but also at creating a new market for agricultural produce, PTI reported. “I challenge anybody to come up with the complaint that his or her vehicle has suffered damage on this account. Of course, those with vested interests may have some other story to tell,” Gadkari said, according to PTI. Read more - Back on voter list? EC orders special drive for left-out, new voters in states where SIR over Gadkari on ethanol blending: 'Show me one damaged vehicle' Gadkari said around 4 crore four-wheelers and 20 crore two-wheelers had been running on petrol blended with ethanol since 2022. Live Events He also said leading automobile manufacturers had tested vehicles with higher ethanol blends, including vehicles capable of running on 100% ethanol. Read more - Running water trains: Railways ready to transport water to drought-hit Maharashtra, but state must first find a water source “Of course, we are importing (conventional fuel) worth Rs 22 lakh crore, and those who feel that their business will get hit are bound to feel bad. But let me tell you, I am the minister in charge of the department concerned; all leading automobile brands have tried running their vehicles even on 100 per cent ethanol. And there have been no complaints,” he said. Ethanol policy aims to diversify farm income Gadkari said the ethanol-blending programme should also be viewed as an agricultural diversification initiative. “We must understand that the decision to blend ethanol with petrol was taken with a view to diversification of agriculture towards energy and power sectors... Our farmers shall no longer remain ‘anna data’ (food producers) but also become ‘urja data’ (energy producers),” he said. The minister said ethanol production from crops such as corn had opened an additional source of income for farmers. According to Gadkari, the use of corn for ethanol had resulted in additional earnings of up to Rs 45,000 crore for farmers in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. “After the Union government took the decision to make ethanol out of corn and the same was used for the aforementioned purposes, it resulted in additional earnings of up to Rs 45,000 crore for farmers of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. Is it not preferable to serve the interests of those from whom we import (fuel),” he asked. Gadkari highlights alternative fuel push Gadkari also cited other efforts to develop alternative fuels and said agricultural waste could be used to produce aviation fuel. “We have even made aviation fuel with rice straw. The future belongs to innovation, technology and research. And a state like Bihar has to play a key role in this direction,” he said.

bihar_raw_news.title: SC grants eight weeks to Bihar to remove encroachments from Ganga flood plains in Patna
bihar_raw_news.content: SC grants eight weeks to Bihar to remove encroachments from Ganga flood plains in Patna Supreme Court gives Bihar 8 weeks to remove all unauthorized structures and encroachments on Ganga flood plains between Nauzar Ghat and Nurpur Ghat in Patna. By PTI October 2, 2026, 3:49:37 PM IST (Updated) 3 Min Read The Supreme Court has granted eight weeks to the Bihar government to comply with its directions to remove all unauthorised structures and encroachments on the flood plains between Nauzar Ghat and Nurpur Ghat in Patna. A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan noted that on July 21, the apex court had granted six weeks to the state to ensure that each and every unauthorised structure and encroachments standing on the Ganga flood plains between Nauzar Ghat and Nurpur Ghat were removed. On September 28, Bihar’s Advocate General S D Sanjay informed the bench that directions issued by the top court were partially complied with. He said the recent natural calamity in Nepal, which led to the level of River Ganga rising, submerged this entire portion and made it difficult for the authorities to proceed further with the removal of encroachments. ”We grant for one last time, eight weeks’ time period to comply with our directions, failing which we shall have to summon the chief secretary of the State of Bihar and other authorities before us and we may also proceed further with contempt,” the bench said. ”After eight weeks, i.e., on the next date of hearing, we want a full compliance report as regards the removal of the encroachments as directed by us. No further time shall be granted,” it said. The top court was hearing a petition challenging a June 2020 order of the National Green Tribunal which had dismissed a plea against illegal constructions and permanent encroachments on the eco-fragile flood plains. In its September 28 order, the bench noted that some intervention applications were filed before it in the matter and these intervenors have said that whatever construction was there, was on their own land and those do not fall within the flood plains. ”In this regard, it may be open for these intervenors to prefer an appropriate representation addressed to the competent authority,” the bench said. The top court said if any representation is preferred by any of the intervenors before it, they shall attach all documents of title over the land, including the authorised sanction and authorisation of building that might have been granted for the purpose of construction. ”In the absence of these documents, no representation shall be looked into,” it said, while disposing of the intervention applications. While hearing the matter in July, the top court had observed that illegal constructions along River Ganga was a matter of concern. It had directed the Bihar government to remove all unauthorised structures and encroachments between Nauzar Ghat and Nurpur Ghat along the river banks within six weeks. bihar_raw_news.title: PMFME Scheme Clears ₹116 Crore for Maharashtra Food Units
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News PMFME Scheme Clears ₹116 Crore for Maharashtra Food Units Breaking News PMFME Scheme Clears ₹116 Crore for Maharashtra Food Units By Urban Acres October 2, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp The PMFME scheme has received approval for ₹116 crore in subsidies for eligible micro food-processing enterprises in Maharashtra, with the funding expected to support projects across the state and strengthen its small-scale processing economy. The approved amount is ₹116 crore, ₹16 lakh and ₹667, with the Centre contributing 60% and the Maharashtra government providing the remaining 40%, according to a report by Loksatta. Maharashtra has established 32,615 projects under the Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises scheme, the report said. The state has been among the leading performers in implementing the scheme since its launch, with food-processing projects spread across several districts. The approval relates to the second instalment for eligible enterprises during the 2026-27 financial year. The central share of the instalment had reportedly been received around 15 days before the approval, while the state government subsequently deposited its 40% contribution. The combined amount has now been approved for distribution to beneficiaries. The funding structure places the release of subsidy support within a shared administrative and financial responsibility between the Union and state governments. While the Centre provides the larger share of the assistance, the state contribution is required before the combined instalment can be distributed to eligible units. The scheme’s implementation has also created a measurable network of small food-processing projects across Maharashtra. These projects are relevant to the state’s district-level economy because they connect local production with processing activity, although the report does not provide a district-wise breakdown of the approved subsidy amount or details of individual beneficiaries. At the national level, Bihar has moved ahead of Maharashtra in the total number of projects established under the scheme, with 34,092 projects, according to the report. Uttar Pradesh has 28,739 projects and Tamil Nadu has 20,407. Maharashtra’s total stands at 32,615 projects. District-level figures show strong representation from Maharashtra among the scheme’s leading locations. Patna in Bihar has the highest number, with 2,745 projects. Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar follows with 2,672, while Sangli has 2,575. The report said seven of the 10 highest-performing districts in the country are in Maharashtra. After Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and Sangli, the Maharashtra districts identified among the leading performers are Ahilyanagar, Nashik, Satara, Kolhapur and Amravati. Their inclusion indicates that the scheme’s reach is not limited to the state’s largest metropolitan centres and extends across districts with established agricultural and food-production activity. The immediate next step is the distribution of the approved second instalment to eligible enterprises after the Centre and Maharashtra have completed their respective funding contributions. The report does not specify the release date for individual beneficiaries or the subsidy amount assigned to each project. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar has immense potential to emerge as major investment hub: Nitin Gadkari - ANI News
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar has immense potential to emerge as major investment hub: Nitin Gadkari ANI | Updated: Oct 02, 2026 08:50 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna ( Bihar ) [India], October 2 (ANI): Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari on Thursday highlighted Bihar 's expanding infrastructure, improved connectivity, skilled human capital and strengthening investment ecosystem, saying the state has immense potential to emerge as a major hub for industry, enterprise and innovation. Gadkari was addressing the Rising Bihar Investor Summit 2026, themed "The Emerging Investment Destination of India", in Patna in the presence of Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary. The Union Minister underlined the importance of infrastructure and connectivity in supporting Bihar 's economic transformation, saying the state's development of roads and other infrastructure can strengthen access to markets, facilitate industrial activity and create employment opportunities. The Centre has also assured support for infrastructure development in Bihar , with Gadkari highlighting the role of road connectivity in supporting investment and economic growth in the state. The Rising Bihar Investor Summit was organised at Hotel Taj City Centre in Patna and brought together policymakers, investors, industry leaders, entrepreneurs and other stakeholders to discuss the state's investment opportunities and industrial growth roadmap. The summit focused on Bihar 's emerging opportunities across sectors, including industry, energy and power, urban development and housing, roads and connectivity, agriculture and food processing, and IT and IT-enabled services. The event also showcased the state's investment incentives and industrial infrastructure. The Bihar Industrial Investment Promotion Package 2025 provides fiscal benefits, subsidies and land concessions for eligible projects, while the state has highlighted more than 100 industrial areas as part of its efforts to attract investment. Gadkari said a prosperous and progressive Bihar would have an important role in advancing the vision of a Viksit Bharat, powered by investment, employment, infrastructure and inclusive economic growth. He emphasised that investment-led development, combined with infrastructure expansion and employment generation, could strengthen Bihar 's position in India's broader economic growth story. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, who was present at the summit, invited domestic and international investors to participate in Bihar 's development journey and assured them of government support. The state government has set an ambitious target of attracting investments worth Rs 5 lakh crore by November this year, according to the summit's official website. Choudhary has also highlighted infrastructure development, industrial expansion and employment generation as key priorities, while encouraging industries to establish manufacturing units in Bihar . The summit's investment-focused agenda included sectoral sessions, business-to-government and business-to-business meetings, policy and incentive showcases, industrial infrastructure presentations, startup and innovation initiatives, and district-level investment opportunities. (ANI)

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated Lovlina Borgohain on winning Gold in the Women’s 75 kg boxing event at the Asian Games. In a series of social media posts, Mr Modi said that her sporting journey reflects remarkable determination and excellence. The Prime Minister has also congratulated Nethra Kumanan on winning the Bronze Medal in the Women’s Dinghy event. He said this is indeed a great accomplishment for India. Prime Minister Modi further congratulated the Indian Men’s Quadrant Team on winning the Bronze Medal at the Asian Games. PM Modi said that this is India’s first-ever medal in the Men’s Quadrant event at the Games. He highlighted that their determination and fighting spirit are exemplary. The Prime Minister extended congratulations to Parveen on winning the Women’s 65kg Boxing Gold after a hard-fought final. He lauded her achievement, saying that it adds another glorious chapter to Indian boxing. PM Modi noted that her success is motivating and highlighted her dedication to sporting excellence. He also congratulated Ankush on winning the Men’s 80kg Boxing Gold with an emphatic victory in the final. Mr Modi said that Ankush’s passion and dedication are noteworthy. He congratulated Sujeet Kalkal on winning the Men’s 65kg Freestyle Wrestling Gold. The Prime Minister commended that on his Asian Games debut, Sujeet has delivered India’s first Wrestling Gold of this edition. PM Modi said that the people of India are rejoicing in the success of the Women’s Hockey Team, who brought home the coveted Gold at the Asian Games and that too after over 4 decades. Praising the team, he said that this is the result of outstanding skills and teamwork, and their determination is very inspiring. national_raw_news.content: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said the Global Horticulture Hub will strengthen the horticulture sector and create better opportunities for farmers in the Rayalaseema region of Andhra Pradesh. Ms Sitharaman laid the foundation stone for the Rayalaseema Global Horticulture Hub project and the Indian School of Agriculture at Madanapalle in Annamayya district today. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan were present on the occasion. Speaking at the event, the Finance Minister said the Centre and the State are working together to develop Andhra Pradesh as a major horticulture centre. She stressed the need for better water management, modern technology and infrastructure to support farmers and improve their incomes. The Finance Minister highlighted Central Government schemes, including PM-KISAN, crop insurance and PM-KUSUM. She also said climate-resilient crop varieties and solar-powered farm pumps are being promoted. The Union Minister said the Indian School of Agriculture will help farmers adopt modern technology, scientific methods and research. She expressed hope that the institution will develop into a world-class centre. The Global Horticulture Hub will cover ten districts and promote crops including mango, banana, tomato and pomegranate. The project will be implemented in three phases, with an estimated investment of about one lakh crore rupees.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | Regional News 48 Goa: Seva Sankalp Abhiyan programme highlights initiatives for self-reliance, agriculture & ...
national_raw_news.content: A programme highlighting initiatives for self-reliance, agriculture and women’s empowerment took place in Ponda, Goa, under the State Government’s Seva Sankalp Abhiyan. Union Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Union Minister of State for Power Shripad Naik and Chief Minister Dr Pramod Sawant attended the programme. Union Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said around 6000 Lakhpati Didis in Goa will be supported to expand their economic activities, with the aim of helping them achieve higher incomes. Mr Chouhan also announced that a third Krishi Vigyan Kendra will be established in Goa in the Kushavati district. He said the government will extend necessary support to farmers and women associated with Self-Help Groups to strengthen their livelihoods. The Minister said the government is making extra efforts, like new plantations, to increase coconut production, which is getting affected due to ageing trees. Chief Minister Dr Pramod Sawant said Goa, known primarily for tourism and mining, is now developing a new identity as a state producing a variety of quality agricultural products. He said around 52 thousand farmers in Goa are engaged in cultivation of different crops. The Chief Minister said around 80 crore rupees were distributed at the programme for various initiatives. Dr Sawant said Swayampurna Goa is taking shape through the combined strength of women, farmers and the people of the state. The Goa Fresh brand was also launched at the programme. The brand aims to promote agricultural products produced by farmers in Goa. A policy for Farmer Producer Organisations was released, and agricultural subsidies were distributed to beneficiaries. A Memorandum of Understanding was signed between the Agriculture Department and the National Institute of Hydrology. The Startup Village Entrepreneurship Programme was launched to promote rural entrepreneurship and women’s empowerment. Lakhpati Didis were felicitated, while financial assistance was provided to Self-Help Groups and approval orders for pink electric rickshaws were distributed. Petrol-powered water pumps were distributed to farmers for irrigation, while medicines and mineral mixture kits were provided to dairy farmers. Swayampurna Mitras and Gram Panchayats were also felicitated at the programme.

national_raw_news.title: India’s gold rush continues with six gold medals on day 13 at Asian Games 1 hour ago 167
national_raw_news.content: The gold rush continued for India at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as Indian athletes delivered a stellar performance on Day 13, clinching six gold medals in Hockey, Boxing, Wrestling and archery – in a spectacular display of skill, determination and sporting excellence. Indian Women’s Hockey team clinched the gold medal, defeating defending champions China 1-nil in the closely fought final. Lalremsiami Hmarzote scored the decisive lone goal for India, while goalkeeper Savita Punia produced a crucial save from a penalty stroke to preserve the lead and secure the gold medal. The victory marks India’s first women’s hockey gold at the Asian Games in 44 years, ending a long wait for the title. The Women’s Hockey team has also secured a direct berth at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Earlier, Indian wrestler Sujeet Kalkal scripted a remarkable comeback to win the gold medal in the men’s 65-kilogram freestyle event. The 23-year-old Indian produced a stunning fightback in the final, recovering from a 4-9 deficit to defeat Tajikistan’s Abdulmazhid Kudiev 10-9 and clinch the Asian Games title. With this victory, Sujeet has joined the elite company of Yogeshwar Dutt and Bajrang Punia, becoming the third Indian wrestler to win Asian Games gold in the men’s 65-kilogram category. In Boxing, Parveen Hooda won the gold medal in the women’s 65kg category, defeating Chinese Taipei’s Nien-Chin Chen 3-2 in a split decision in the final. Ankush Panghal clinched the gold medal in the men’s 80-kilogram category, defeating South Korea’s Kim Minseong by a split decision, 4-0, in the final. India’s star woman boxer Lovlina Borgohain also clinched a gold medal in the 75kg category, defeating China’s Bao Ziyi by a unanimous 5-0 decision in the final. It is India’s second gold medal in women’s boxing at the Asian Games, following Mary Kom’s gold in 2014. In archery, the women’s recurve team created history by clinching its maiden Asian Games gold medal. The trio of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod defeated world champions South Korea 5-3 in a thrilling final. India also bagged silver in the mixed recurve team event. Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara finished runners-up after going down 3-5 to China in a closely contested final. In Sepaktakraw, India secured the bronze medal in the men’s quadrant event. The Indian team lost 0-2 to Japan in the semi-final but earned a place on the podium. In Sailing, Nethra Kumanan clinched bronze in the women’s dinghy event. The 29-year-old Indian sailor finished third with an overall score of 14 points. With these impressive performances, India has climbed to fifth position in the overall medal standings. The country’s medal tally has risen to 76, including 16 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze medals.

national_raw_news.title: CBN Jaipur seizes over 1 kg of hydroponic weed concealed in Thailand parcel 2 hours ago 38
national_raw_news.content: The Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN), Jaipur, has seized more than one kilogram of hydroponic weed concealed in an international parcel from Thailand at the Foreign Post Office, Jaipur. The Finance Ministry said the contraband was concealed in 29 pouches of cakes and mixed with other articles to camouflage it. The weed was seized under the relevant provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS Act), 1985. On the other hand, the Madhya Pradesh unit of the Bureau has seized over four kilograms of opium packed in two packets from a motorcycle on the Kanjarda-Manasa road and arrested one person based on specific intelligence. The Madhya Pradesh Unit also destroyed more than 10 thousand 842 kilograms of seized narcotic drugs at Khor, Madhya Pradesh, through the authorised disposal process under the NDPS Act, 1985. The operation was conducted under the watch of the Drug Disposal Committee and in the presence of an MP Pollution Control Board representative. The CBN further deposited over 154 kilograms of seized opium at the Government Opium and Alkaloid Works, Neemuch, as part of the disposal process. The Ministry said that the destruction or disposal of seized narcotic drugs is undertaken by CBN in accordance with the applicable provisions and prescribed procedures, ensuring that seized contraband does not re-enter the illicit drug trafficking network and is incinerated in an environmentally.
